overall: As of 4:52 AM ET, NYC is at 86°F with clear skies and calm winds, coming off an overnight running max of 90.0°F reached at 00:51 ET. Temperatures have been declining at roughly 1°F/hr since that overnight peak, which is normal pre-dawn radiative cooling ahead of what is forecast to be an extreme heat day. An Extreme Heat Warning is in effect through Saturday 9 PM with dangerous heat index values of 105–115°F expected.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in very strong agreement on an intense daytime peak: GFS and ECMWF both at 104.2°F, HRRR at 103.6°F, and NBM slightly lower at 101.3°F — all converging on a ~4 PM peak hour. However, the fused META model distributes nearly all probability across just 90–95°F (33.3% each in three consecutive even buckets), which stands in stark contrast to the NWS 102°F call and NWP consensus, suggesting a possible intraday calibration artifact or regime uncertainty at this very early morning hour.
max_temp_prediction: With clear skies, an active Extreme Heat Warning, and all major NWP models clustering between 101–104°F, the NWS forecast of near 102°F carries strong credibility for today's daytime high. The INTRADAY model (which is early and obs-driven) places meaningful probability in the 96–102°F range, broadly supportive of triple-digit heat. For the active even-bucket Kalshi market, probability is diffuse — the top bucket is only 90–91F at 11.6% — reflecting genuine model spread, but the ensemble recommendation is to skip. Best estimate is approximately 102°F, with moderate-to-high confidence in triple digits but real uncertainty around whether the final peak lands in the 100–102 or 102–105 range.
